There are traps on the Week 2 waiver wire, and there are claims worth making. The line between them is age and role. A receiver who is 24 years old and flashed in 2025 is worth a real bid. A tight end drafted in 2018 who just had his best game in years is not, no matter what the Week 1 box score says.
One more thing before the names. We just launched our Waiver Wire tool that gives you recommended waiver wire moves for your specific league.

Coker is the top claim in most leagues, and the ankle is the first thing to settle. He walked out of the opener in a boot and called it a tweak, and by Monday, September 14 the reporting had him day to day and on track to play in Week 2. Add him with that in mind, and keep an eye on the practice report.
The reason to bid is the depth chart, not one box score. Carolina has no tight end of note and no third receiver of relevance, so the targets behind Tetairoa McMillan have nowhere else to go, and Coker already showed this ceiling in 2025 with 134 yards against the Rams in the game that mattered most. I would not start him at Atlanta in Week 2 with the Falcons’ quarterback situation unsettled, but one more game like the opener and he is a Week 3 starter.

The question all summer was whether Jordan James or Kaelon Black would be the running back behind Christian McCaffrey, and Black answered it in the opener. With James nursing fractured ribs, Black was out-carrying McCaffrey while the game was still close, and McCaffrey’s snap share was the lowest of any game he has played healthy in San Francisco.
None of that makes Black startable on his own. What it makes him is one of the premium handcuffs in the league, because every time McCaffrey has missed time, whoever Kyle Shanahan hands the job to has been a top 10 running back. If you picked up Mike Washington during the Jeanty scare, this is the swap.

Mayer is probably rostered in your league after the Brock Bowers injury, but if he is not, he is the tight end to add. Las Vegas ran away from Miami and had little reason to throw, and Mayer still drew targets at a rate that holds up when the game script flips.
Week 2 is where it flips. The Raiders play the Chargers, who just let Trey McBride run wild, and a game the Raiders trail is a game where the passes go to Mayer in the second half. With Kyle Pitts and Colston Loveland both giving their managers nothing in the opener, there are plenty of lineups where Mayer is the better Week 2 play.

DEEPER LEAGUES
Romeo Doubs  WR · NE
Week 1 at SEA: 3 targets · 0 receptions · 0 yards · 0.0 PPR
Scored 0 in the opener and is still the receiver I would hold in New England, because A.J. Brown is out until at least Week 6 with a high ankle sprain and somebody has to be the WR1. A bench piece for deeper leagues, not a league winner, and the one I would take over DeMario Douglas.
Pat Bryant  WR · DEN
Week 1 at KC: 6 targets · 4 receptions · 42 yards · 8.2 PPR
Denver kept throwing his way on Monday, September 14 while Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle did next to nothing, and I moved him up to WR55 on my board. Worth a roster spot in deeper leagues, not a start, until the role holds for more than one game.
DON’T CHASE
Devaughn Vele  WR · NO
Week 1 at DET: 9 targets · 7 receptions · 69 yards · 19.9 PPR
The Saints only dropped back 60 times because Detroit forced them to and the game went to overtime. He is 28 years old with under 800 receiving yards for his entire career, and that passing volume is not coming back most weeks.
Mike Gesicki  TE · CIN
Week 1 vs TB: 7 targets · 5 receptions · 78 yards · 18.8 PPR
One good game against Tampa Bay from a tight end drafted in 2018, now 30 years old, who had about 300 receiving yards all of last season. It is a random Week 1 performance, not a breakout. Let your leaguemates chase him.
Demarcus Robinson  WR · SF
Week 1 at LAR: 3 targets · 2 receptions · 50 yards · 13.0 PPR
De’Zhaun Stribling is out for a while and Robinson looked good in his place, but he is 31 years old and has never been relevant in fantasy. Do not spend a claim on him.
Tyler Shough  QB · NO
Week 1 at DET: 410 passing yards · 3 passing TDs · 8 rushing yards · 23.2 PPR
The yardage came from about 60 dropbacks, an overtime drive, and he barely ran. Until Jordyn Tyson is back in that offense the ceiling is capped, and Shough is not the quarterback I would stream in Week 2.
George Holani  RB · SEA
Week 1 vs NE: 8 carries · 29 rushing yards · 1 target · 2.9 PPR
He split the Seattle backfield with Jadarian Price in the opener, and even if Price went down I would expect a committee with Emanuel Wilson rather than a workhorse. Let somebody else use the roster spot on him.
DEFENSES TO STREAM
My pick: 49ers vs Dolphins
San Francisco is the biggest favorite on the Week 2 slate, and Miami is projected for one of the lowest point totals of any offense. A lead like that is where the sacks and the interceptions come from. If they are on your wire, they are the defense to claim.
Also in play
Eagles vs Titans · Buccaneers vs Browns · Chargers vs Raiders
How I pick them
I stream defenses off the betting markets: the biggest spread on the slate and the lowest projected total for the other offense. My own Week 2 start is the Chargers against the Raiders, even after their opener.
